*Supersedes the version effective 1 January 2025. 'Should' becomes 'must', reflecting the legal requirement more precisely.*

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how Alderbridge Care Group checks a new starter's right to work in the UK. It applies to every new starter at every site.

Policy statement

HR must check right-to-work documents before a new starter's first day — no employee may start work without this check having been completed and recorded — meeting Alderbridge's legal obligation to confirm every employee is legally entitled to work before they begin.

Definitions

**Right-to-work check** the document check confirming a person's legal entitlement to work in the UK, following the current Home Office guidance on acceptable document types, now a mandatory precondition to starting work rather than an expected best practice. **Document retention copy** the copy of the checked document retained as evidence the check was completed correctly.

1. Request the required right-to-work document from a new starter as soon as an offer is accepted, allowing time to complete the mandatory check before their first day.
2. Check the original document in person, or via the Home Office's online right-to-work checking service where applicable, following current guidance on acceptable evidence.
3. Retain a copy of the checked document, dated and annotated to confirm when and how the check was completed.
4. No employee may start work without this check having been completed and recorded; this is now an absolute requirement, a tightening from the previous version's advisory wording.

Video calls and screen sharing while working remotely

During a video call or screen share involving sensitive information, staff confirm no unauthorised person can view or overhear the call, close any unrelated sensitive document before sharing a screen, and use only Alderbridge-approved conferencing tools rather than a personal account on an unapproved platform, applying the same care to a video meeting as to an in-person conversation about the same information.

Wi-Fi security at an approved home location

Home Wi-Fi used for Alderbridge work is secured with a strong, unique password and up-to-date router firmware, and an entirely open or default-password network is not used for any Alderbridge system; where genuinely uncertain about home network security, IT can advise on basic steps to improve it.

Ending a remote working arrangement

Where a remote working arrangement ends, whether by the employee's own request or a genuine business need, IT confirms the issued device and any remote access credential are returned or revoked promptly, following the same access-removal discipline the IT Acceptable Use Policy sets out for a leaver, since a remote arrangement ending is functionally similar to a change of access requirement even where employment itself continues.

Backing up work created while working remotely

Family members and household members during remote work

A family or household member should never have access to an Alderbridge device or account, even briefly and even for an unrelated purpose such as checking their own personal email, since this creates an unnecessary and entirely avoidable risk to data the household member has no reason to see.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how Alderbridge Care Group responds to a reference request for a current or

Policy statement

HR provides a factual reference confirming dates of employment and job title within 5 working days of a
request, tightened from the previous 10 working days, giving a former or current staff member a faster,

Definitions

**Factual reference** a reference limited to objective facts such as dates of employment and job title, as

Roles and responsibilities

**HR** processes every reference request and issues the factual reference within the tightened

request.

request being received, a tightening from the previous 10-working-day standard.

3. Limit the reference to factual, objective information; a subjective opinion on the staff member's
performance or conduct is not included.

4. Direct a request for a fuller, opinion-based reference to the registered manager, who decides whether
and how to respond to that specific, different type of request.

dense_candidates.chunk_text:

What a formal absence review meeting actually covers

A formal absence review meeting triggered at the red level is a genuinely two-way conversation, not a predetermined disciplinary step: it reviews the specific pattern openly, explores whether an underlying cause (health, workplace factors, or personal circumstances) can be identified and addressed, considers whether occupational health input would help, and only where a pattern is not disability-related and shows no sign of improving despite support does it begin to move toward considering whether continued employment in the current role remains sustainable — a possibility discussed transparently rather than left unspoken while informally already decided.

Confidentiality of health information disclosed during absence management

Any health information an employee shares as part of a return-to-work discussion or a formal absence review is treated as confidential, shared only with those who genuinely need to know (for example, HR and, where a reasonable adjustment is agreed, the employee's own line manager) rather than discussed more widely, and an employee is never expected to disclose more clinical detail than they are comfortable sharing beyond what a fit note or occupational health report already confirms.

Absence during a probationary period

A probationary employee's absence is monitored against the same trigger points, but the shorter probationary window means HR and the line manager review any absence pattern more promptly, since a genuine, sustained concern about attendance reliability is relevant to the eventual probation confirmation decision under the Probationary Period Policy, discussed openly with the employee rather than left unaddressed until the probation end date arrives.

Closing note on tone

Every conversation this policy describes — a return-to-work discussion, an absence review, a trigger-point escalation — is expected to be conducted with genuine warmth and curiosity about what is actually going on for the employee, since a policy applied correctly but coldly achieves compliance without achieving the actual purpose this policy exists for, which is a workplace where people feel able to be honest about being unwell and supported back when they are ready.

Beyond general wellbeing, managers are trained to recognise the specific signs of burnout common in care work — persistent exhaustion not resolved by rest, growing cynicism or detachment from a role someone previously enjoyed, and a sense of reduced personal effectiveness — since burnout often develops gradually and is easy to mistake for an ordinary bad patch until it has become genuinely serious, and early, proactive conversation makes a real difference to how well and how quickly someone recovers.

Worked example

This guidance sets out a thorough, consistent standard, but it is applied with genuine judgement rather than mechanically — a hiring manager who identifies a real concern not explicitly anticipated by this guidance raises it with HR rather than either ignoring it because it does not fit a listed scenario, or refusing to hire on an unexamined suspicion alone, since safer recruitment ultimately depends on people exercising good judgement within a well-designed process, not on the process alone doing all the work.

This procedure sets out how Alderbridge Care Group checks a new starter's right to work in the UK. It applies to every new starter at every site.

Policy statement

HR must check right-to-work documents before a new starter's first day — no employee may start work without this check having been completed and recorded — meeting Alderbridge's legal obligation to confirm every employee is legally entitled to work before they begin.

Definitions

request being received, a tightening from the previous 10-working-day standard.
